outcome: The general Tate conjecture is not settled as of 13 October 2026, and no source I opened says it is. Since 26 January 2024 the abelian-variety case over finite fields has been claimed in 2026 by two live manuscripts: in dimension four by a single-author preprint (Matt Broe, arXiv 2608.28651, 19 August 2026), whose author says a large language model suggested a key method, and in all dimensions by an OpenAI manuscript (catalogue entry 032, released 6 October 2026) in which the Tate statement is a corollary, via Milne's theorems, of an OpenAI-claimed Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties that no qualified mathematician has publicly checked. Two Tate-for-powers-of-abelian-varieties preprints by Ningyi Li (5 and 10 September 2026) were withdrawn on 8 October 2026. Partial cases (surfaces of geometric genus one, abelian varieties with non-maximal angle rank, a few reformulations) appeared in 2024 and 2025, and integral-Tate variants moved in the same period; these are recorded and discounted below.
problem_asks: The statement asks about the Tate conjecture linking algebraic cycles on varieties to Galois representations on étale cohomology. Unpacked, from the statement alone: (1) Tate's first conjecture: for a smooth projective variety X over a finitely generated field k, in every codimension r, and for every prime ℓ not equal to the characteristic, the ℓ-adic cycle class map from CH^r(X)⊗Q_ℓ onto the Galois-invariant part of H^{2r}_ét(X_k̄, Q_ℓ(r)) is surjective, so that Galois-invariant classes are spanned by algebraic cycles. The bullet says 'algebraic varieties'; the standard formulation takes smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields, and I use that. (2) Its codimension-1 (divisor) case, which the literature treats as the central open case. (3) Tate's second conjecture, the number-field half of the name: the rank of the algebraic cycles modulo homological equivalence equals the order of the pole at s = r of the L-function attached to H^{2r}(X)(r). The bullet does not write this out; it is listed because it is the standard second half of the name, and the later pass can decide. The bullet does not restrict to finite fields, abelian varieties, K3 surfaces or surfaces, so each such case is a case of the question. Not included: the strong form (semisimplicity) and the integral or logarithmic variants, which are different questions.

events.what_happened: J. S. Milne, 'Lefschetz classes on abelian varieties' (1999). Shows that if the Hodge conjecture holds for all complex abelian varieties of CM type, then the Tate conjecture (and the standard conjectures) hold for all abelian varieties over finite fields. I took this from Milne's 2021 abstract (arXiv 2112.12815), which says 'the earlier articles showed' it; the 1999 PDF did not load for me, so the statement rests on that description.
events.delivers: A conditional reduction: Tate for all abelian varieties over finite fields, in every codimension, follows from the Hodge conjecture for all complex CM abelian varieties. Conditional on that hypothesis, which was open when Milne's 2021 abstract was written.
events.remains: Everything unconditionally: the reduction proves nothing by itself. Also untouched: non-abelian varieties and Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, conditionally: it reduces that case to Hodge for CM abelian varieties.

events.what_happened: J. S. Milne, 'The Tate Conjecture for Certain Abelian Varieties over Finite Fields', arXiv math/9911218 (27 November 1999). Tate's 1966 theorem covers abelian varieties over finite fields whose algebra of Tate classes is generated by degree-1 classes; Milne constructs families where that condition fails and proves the Tate conjecture for them. The abstract does not state the codimensions or the exact class.
events.delivers: Unconditional Tate for the constructed families of abelian varieties over finite fields, for which the Tate classes are not generated by degree-1 classes. The exact class and codimensions are not in the abstract I read.
events.remains: All other abelian varieties over finite fields; all non-abelian varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for the constructed abelian varieties.

events.what_happened: François Charles, 'The Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finite fields', arXiv 1206.4002 (v1 18 June 2012; v2 7 July 2012). Proves Artin's conjecture on supersingular K3 surfaces over fields of characteristic p > 3, which gives the Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finite fields of characteristic p > 3. Also Tate for divisors on certain holomorphic symplectic varieties (with characteristic restrictions) and codimension-2 Tate for cubic fourfolds over finite fields of characteristic p > 3. A search summary gives Inventiones as the journal; I did not check that.
events.revisions: v2 7 July 2012; the v2 comment says Theorem 4 is stated in greater generality, with unchanged proofs.
events.delivers: The divisor case (Tate I in codimension 1) for K3 surfaces over finite fields of characteristic p > 3; Tate for divisors on certain holomorphic symplectic varieties over finite fields with characteristic restrictions; codimension-2 Tate for cubic fourfolds over finite fields of characteristic p > 3.
events.remains: Characteristics 2 and 3 for K3 surfaces; higher codimensions for K3 surfaces; all other varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for these K3 surfaces and cubic fourfolds in characteristic p > 3.

events.what_happened: Keerthi Madapusi Pera, 'The Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces in odd characteristic', arXiv 1301.6326 (v1 27 January 2013; v2 20 February 2013; v3 4 June 2014). Uses the Kuga–Satake construction, away from characteristic 2, to reduce the Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finitely generated fields of odd characteristic to a statement about a regular integral model of an orthogonal Shimura variety. A search summary gives Inventiones Mathematicae 201 (2015) as the journal; I did not check that.
events.delivers: The Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finitely generated fields of odd characteristic, the divisor case for K3 surfaces. The fetched abstract text also refers to an extension to codimension-2 cycles on cubic fourfolds (per the fetch summary).
events.remains: Characteristic 2; K3-type objects beyond K3 surfaces; all other varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for K3 surfaces over finitely generated fields of odd characteristic.

events.what_happened: Masaki Kameko, 'On the integral Tate conjecture for finite fields', arXiv 1408.2636 (submitted 12 August 2014). Abstract: non-torsion counterexamples to the integral Tate conjecture for finite fields; extends Pirutka and Yagita from the primes 2, 3, 5 to all primes. A search summary gives Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2015); I did not check that.
events.delivers: Non-torsion counterexamples to the integral (not rational) ℓ-adic Tate statement over finite fields, for every prime ℓ. A variant only.
events.remains: Not applicable: this bears on the integral variant. The rational statement in problem_asks is untouched.
events.direction: Against the integral variant (counterexamples there); neutral for the rational conjecture.
events.object: Non-torsion counterexamples to the integral Tate statement over finite fields, one for each prime ℓ. The construction is not described in the abstract I read, so whether it is explicit is not established.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Antieau, 'On the integral Tate conjecture for finite fields and representation theory', arXiv 1504.04879 (v1 19 April 2015; v2 28 May 2015, marked final, 'to appear in Algebraic Geometry'). New counterexamples to the integral Hodge and integral Tate conjectures, given as approximations of the classifying spaces of groups of type A_n; Milnor operations vanish on the classes constructed.
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the integral variant of Tate (and of Hodge), via classifying-space approximations for type-A groups. The abstract gives no primes or degree.
events.remains: Not applicable: a variant.
events.direction: Against the integral variant; neutral for the rational conjecture.
events.object: Counterexample classes in the cohomology of approximations to BG for groups of type A_n, constructed by representation theory; the abstract does not give the specific groups, primes or degree.

events.what_happened: Masaki Kameko, 'Representation theory and the cycle map of a classifying space', arXiv 1601.06199 (v1 22 January 2016; v2 3 July 2016). Computes the Chern subgroup of the degree-4 integral cohomology of a classifying space and shows it is proper, giving new counterexamples to the integral Hodge and Tate conjectures modulo torsion. (A search summary credited this to Tripathy; the fetched abstract names Kameko.)
events.delivers: Counterexamples to the integral Tate statement modulo torsion, a variant. The primes and groups are not given in the abstract.
events.remains: Not applicable: a variant.
events.direction: Against the integral variant modulo torsion; neutral for the rational conjecture.
events.object: A classifying space whose degree-4 integral cohomology has a proper Chern subgroup, so that it yields counterexamples modulo torsion. The abstract does not name the group or the prime.

events.what_happened: Kazuhiro Ito, Tetsushi Ito and Teruhisa Koshikawa, 'CM liftings of K3 surfaces over finite fields and their applications to the Tate conjecture', arXiv 1809.09604 (v1 25 September 2018; v2 25 December 2018). Shows that every K3 surface of finite height over a finite field has a characteristic-0 lifting whose generic fibre is a K3 surface with complex multiplication; with results of Mukai and Buskin, proves the Tate conjecture for the square of a K3 surface over a finite field, for K3 surfaces in all characteristics including 2 and 3. Published in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 9 (2021), e29, online 8 April 2021.
events.revisions: v2 25 December 2018; journal version Forum Math. Sigma 9 (2021) e29, online 8 April 2021.
events.delivers: The Tate conjecture for the square X×X of a K3 surface over a finite field, in all characteristics (abstract: 'including those of characteristic 2 or 3'). Not for higher powers or other varieties.
events.remains: Tate for K3 powers beyond the square; all other varieties; Tate's second conjecture.

checked_by.who: Forum of Mathematics, Sigma (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; the referees are not named in sources I read
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper after peer review

events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for squares of K3 surfaces over finite fields.

events.what_happened: Ziquan Yang, 'The Tate Conjecture for Motivic Endomorphisms of K3 Surfaces over Finite Fields', arXiv 2110.01350 (v1 4 October 2021, the only version). Gives a more geometric proof of the Tate conjecture for squares of K3 surfaces over finite fields when the characteristic is at least 5, using twisted derived equivalences between K3 surfaces.
events.delivers: The Tate conjecture for squares of K3 surfaces over finite fields in characteristic at least 5, by a different route.
events.remains: Characteristics 2 and 3 for this route; other varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for K3 squares in characteristic at least 5.

events.what_happened: J. S. Milne, 'The Tate and Standard Conjectures for Certain Abelian Varieties', arXiv 2112.12815 (v1 23 December 2021; v2 7 February 2022). Reworks the proofs behind his CM-Hodge reduction so that they apply to one abelian variety at a time, and so proves unconditionally the Tate and standard conjectures for many abelian varieties over finite fields, including some whose Tate classes are not generated by divisor classes.
events.delivers: Unconditional Tate (and standard) conjecture for a class of abelian varieties over finite fields, described in the abstract only as 'many' abelian varieties, including some with Tate classes not generated by divisors.
events.remains: Abelian varieties outside that class (the CM-Hodge route would cover all of them if that hypothesis held); non-abelian varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture for a class of abelian varieties over finite fields.

events.what_happened: Chao Li and Wei Zhang, 'A note on Tate's conjectures for abelian varieties', arXiv 2112.15164 (v1 30 December 2021; v2 20 May 2022, minor revisions). Mostly expository: explains a proof of Tate's two conjectures for algebraic cycles of arbitrary codimension on certain products of elliptic curves and abelian surfaces over number fields.
events.delivers: Tate's two conjectures, in all codimensions, for certain products of elliptic curves and abelian surfaces over number fields. The abstract does not say which products.
events.remains: Other products and abelian varieties; finite fields; general varieties.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture for the stated products over number fields.

events.what_happened: Federico Scavia and Fumiaki Suzuki, 'Non-algebraic geometrically trivial cohomology classes over finite fields', arXiv 2206.12732 (v1 25 June 2022; v2 15 April 2023; v3 23 September 2024, final, 'to appear in Advances in Mathematics'). Constructs smooth projective varieties over a finite field with a torsion ℓ-adic degree-4 class that is not algebraic but vanishes over the algebraic closure (some are fourfolds). Shows that two versions of the integral Tate conjecture over a finite field are not equivalent.
events.revisions: v2 15 April 2023; v3 23 September 2024 (final, to appear in Advances in Mathematics).
events.delivers: Counterexamples to integral (torsion) ℓ-adic Tate statements over finite fields, and the separation of two integral versions. A variant only.
events.remains: Not applicable: a variant.
events.direction: Against integral variants; no bearing on the rational statement.
events.object: Smooth projective varieties over a finite field carrying a torsion degree-4 ℓ-adic class that is not algebraic but dies over the algebraic closure; some examples are fourfolds. The abstract does not say whether the construction is explicit.

events.what_happened: Paul Hamacher, Ziquan Yang and Xiaolei Zhao, 'On the Tate conjecture for divisors on varieties with h^{2,0} = 1 in positive characteristics', arXiv 2207.11904 (v1 25 July 2022; v4 30 May 2025, marked final, 'to appear in Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik'). Proves that the Tate conjecture for divisors holds generically for mod p reductions of complex projective varieties with h^{2,0} = 1, under a mild assumption on moduli; gives a new BSD case over global function fields and the Tate conjecture for a class of general-type surfaces of geometric genus 1.
events.revisions: v2 2 May 2023; v3 22 August 2023; v4 30 May 2025 (final; the title was reverted from an earlier version).
events.delivers: The divisor case of Tate, 'generically', for mod p reductions of complex projective varieties with h^{2,0} = 1 under a mild assumption on moduli (the abstract does not state it precisely); the divisor case for a class of general-type surfaces of geometric genus 1.
events.remains: Reductions outside the generic locus and under the excluded assumption; varieties with h^{2,0} ≠ 1; codimensions above 1; Tate's second conjecture.
events.doubts: The arXiv comment says 'to appear' in Crelle, so acceptance is stated but the refereeing is not checked here. The abstract says 'generically' without defining it.
events.direction: Toward the divisor case, generically.

events.what_happened: Stefan Schreieder, 'Remarks on Milnor K-theory and Tate's conjecture for divisors', arXiv 2406.18706 (v1 26 June 2024; v2 8 December 2024, marked final, 'to appear in Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici'). Shows that the Tate conjecture for divisors over a finite field F is equivalent to an explicit algebraic problem about the third Milnor K-group of the function field F̄(x,y,z).
events.delivers: An equivalence: the divisor case of Tate over finite fields holds if and only if a stated problem about K^M_3 of F̄(x,y,z) holds. The abstract does not claim to settle either side.
events.remains: The divisor case over finite fields (the equivalent problem is not resolved in the abstract); higher codimensions; number fields; Tate's second conjecture.
events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation that neither confirms nor refutes the divisor case.

events.what_happened: Fumiaki Suzuki, talk with Federico Scavia, 'The integral Tate conjecture over finite fields and two coniveau filtrations'. Per the talk abstract (seen in search results, not opened): a new type of counterexample to the integral Tate conjecture over finite fields, where a geometric cycle map is surjective but an arithmetic cycle map is not, plus positive results toward a conjecture of Colliot-Thélène and Kahn. First seen as an October 2024 talk; later talk listings are dated November and December 2025. No paper located.
events.delivers: Per the talk abstract only: counterexamples to an integral variant over finite fields. Nothing about the rational statement.
events.remains: Not applicable: a variant.
events.doubts: Known only from talk listings seen in search results; the talk pages were not opened and no paper was located, so the content cannot be checked here.
events.direction: Against the integral variant, if the abstract is right; neutral for the rational conjecture.
events.object: A new type of counterexample to the integral Tate statement over finite fields, described in the abstract only as a case where the geometric cycle map is surjective and the arithmetic one is not. Not described further in anything I read.

events.what_happened: Anna Cadoret and Alena Pirutka, 'Uniform bounds for obstructions to the integral Tate conjecture', arXiv 2410.21010 (v1, the only version, 28 October 2024). Assuming natural variational realization conjectures, gives uniform bounds on the obstruction to the integral Tate conjecture in one-dimensional families of varieties over an infinite finitely generated field.
events.delivers: Conditional bounds on the failure of the integral Tate statement in one-parameter families, conditional on the stated variational realization conjectures, which are not proved here. An integral variant.
events.remains: Not applicable to the rational statement; the conditional hypotheses remain open as far as the abstract says.
events.doubts: The result is conditional on hypotheses that the abstract names but does not spell out, and none of them is established in the paper's abstract.
events.direction: Neutral for the rational conjecture; bounds on an integral obstruction, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Haoyang Guo and Ziquan Yang, 'The Tate conjecture for surfaces of geometric genus one -- embracing singularities', arXiv 2501.18541 (v1 30 January 2025; v2 11 June 2025, marked 'major revision'). Aims to largely complete the programme of proving the Tate conjecture for surfaces of geometric genus one, by treating surfaces whose natural models are singular. Application: every elliptic curve of height one over a genus-one global function field of characteristic p ≥ 11 satisfies the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.
events.revisions: v2 11 June 2025, 'major revision'; the abstract page gives no list of changes.
events.delivers: The divisor case of Tate for a large part of surfaces of geometric genus one. 'Largely complete' means not all of that class; the characteristic restriction for the Tate part is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The residual surfaces of geometric genus one that the programme does not yet reach (not listed in the abstract); other surfaces; higher codimensions; Tate's second conjecture.
events.doubts: The abstract says 'largely complete', so the residual cases are not covered by the claim; the v2 'major revision' is not described in what I read.
events.direction: Toward the divisor case for a large class of surfaces; not the full class.

events.what_happened: Eyal Markman, 'Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds', arXiv 2502.03415 (v1 5 February 2025; v2 8 June 2025). A Hodge-side result, not Tate: proves Weil classes are algebraic on abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant −1, for all imaginary quadratic fields; via a degeneration argument of Schoen, extends to abelian fourfolds of Weil type, and the abstract says this gives the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds.
events.delivers: The Hodge conjecture for Weil-type abelian sixfolds of discriminant −1 and fourfolds of Weil type, per the abstract. It says nothing directly about Tate classes.
events.remains: Every part of problem_asks: this is a different question (Hodge), and the Tate statement is not addressed.
events.direction: On the Hodge side; neutral for the Tate statement itself.

events.what_happened: Kazuya Kato, Chikara Nakayama and Sampei Usui, 'Logarithmic Tate conjectures over finite fields', arXiv 2502.16974 (v1 24 February 2025). Formulates an analogue of the Tate conjecture for log geometry over a finite field; shows the weight-monodromy conjecture follows from it together with semisimplicity of Frobenius.
events.delivers: An analogue only: a logarithmic version. The abstract says it does not prove the analogue.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, which is a different question here.
events.direction: Not about the bullet's statement; an analogue.

events.what_happened: Bruno Kahn, 'An approach to the Tate conjecture for surfaces over a finite field', arXiv 2505.07337 (v1, the only version, 12 May 2025). Reformulates the Tate conjecture for a surface over a finite field in terms of suitable affine open subsets; gives three attempts to prove the reformulation, each of which, per the abstract, falls short.
events.delivers: A reformulation only. No case is proved; the abstract says the three attempts fall short.
events.remains: All of problem_asks for surfaces over finite fields.
events.direction: Neutral: a reformulation with no proved case.

events.what_happened: Santiago Arango-Piñeros, Sam Frengley and Sameera Vemulapalli, 'Galois groups of simple abelian varieties over finite fields and exceptional Tate classes', arXiv 2505.09589 (v1, the only version, 14 May 2025). Proves new cases of the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, including cases where the angle rank is non-maximal; gives a combinatorial criterion for exceptional Tate classes on geometrically simple abelian varieties with commutative endomorphism algebra; an algorithm relates Newton polygons and CM fields. Talks: Washington (May 2025) and Bristol (February 2026); talks are not verification.
events.delivers: New cases of Tate I for certain geometrically simple abelian varieties over finite fields, identified by Galois group and Newton-polygon data. The abstract does not list the codimensions covered.
events.remains: All other abelian varieties over finite fields; non-abelian varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.doubts: I read the abstract page only. The cases are given by a criterion whose scope I did not check in the full text.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture for new cases of abelian varieties over finite fields.

events.what_happened: Matt Broe, 'The Beilinson–Bloch conjecture for some non-isotrivial varieties over global function fields', arXiv 2509.03602 (v1 3 September 2025). Proves Beilinson–Bloch for certain classes of non-isotrivial varieties over global function fields; derives Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer for intermediate Jacobians of these; the abstract says these results establish 'new cases of the Tate conjecture over finite fields'. The abstract does not list the cases.
events.delivers: New cases of the Tate conjecture over finite fields, for the non-isotrivial varieties covered (over F_q(t)), derived from BSD-type statements for their intermediate Jacobians that the paper proves for those classes. The cases are not spelled out in the abstract.
events.remains: Tate for varieties outside those classes; general varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.doubts: I read the abstract only. The same author posted the 2026 abelian-fourfold preprint, so this paper's status is not independent of that author's later work.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture for the classes covered.

events.what_happened: J. S. Milne, 'On the integral Tate conjecture for abelian varieties', arXiv 2509.06707 (v1, the only version, 8 September 2025). Using Engel et al. (2025), who showed that the integral Hodge conjecture fails for very general abelian varieties, and Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles, deduces a similar failure for the integral Tate conjecture.
events.delivers: A failure of the integral Tate statement for (some) abelian varieties, per the abstract; the fields, degree and exact form are not in the abstract.
events.remains: The rational statement in problem_asks.
events.direction: Against the integral variant only; does not touch the rational conjecture.
events.object: A failure of the integral Tate statement for abelian varieties, deduced from Engel et al.'s failure of the integral Hodge conjecture for very general abelian varieties. Non-constructive in form (deduced), and the specific varieties are not given in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Tony Feng, 'Steenrod operations and symplectic arithmetic duality', arXiv 2602.15629 (v1 17 February 2026). Expository: introduces a conjecture from Tate's 1966 Bourbaki report predicting a symplectic form on Brauer groups of surfaces over finite fields, and gives an informal tour of the proofs in two cited works.
events.delivers: Expository; the abstract states no new result. It concerns Brauer groups, an analogue with a symplectic form, not Tate's conjecture for algebraic cycles.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Not about the bullet's statement; a Brauer-group analogue.

events.what_happened: Matt Broe, 'The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields', arXiv 2608.28651 (v1, the only version as of 13 October 2026, submitted 19 August 2026; sole author). Abstract: proves the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields, 'the first resolution of the conjecture for all abelian varieties of a fixed dimension over finite fields since the work of Tate in the 1960s'. Uses techniques from Ancona's proof of the standard conjecture of Hodge type for abelian fourfolds and ultimately reduces to Markman's results on algebraicity of Weil classes; with Ancona and Kahn's theorems, deduces the standard conjecture D for abelian fourfolds over arbitrary fields. Acknowledgements thank Giuseppe Ancona for comments. Disclosure (arXiv HTML, quoted via a fetch tool): 'A large language model was used in the preparation of this manuscript to explore proof strategies, to locate relevant literature, to critically examine mathematical arguments, and to assist with copyediting and LaTeX typesetting.' The author first asked the model to try to use Markman's results to prove Theorem 1.1; the model then suggested a method involving Ancona's analysis of exotic classes and the 'stabilization' idea (Remark 1.4); the author then developed it, 'significantly restructured it, identified and corrected a number of errors and gaps', and based the proof on the theory of Chow motives with a motivic technique. The model is not named: a footnote says the author opted not to identify it, 'for reasons similar to those given in' a prior paper's footnote (which I did not resolve). Second disclosure paragraph: 'All mathematical statements and cited references in the manuscript were independently checked by the author.'
events.revisions: None as of 13 October 2026 (only v1 is listed).
events.delivers: Tate I for abelian fourfolds over finite fields: for an abelian fourfold A over a field k (the fetched HTML text says 'over a field k'; the title and abstract say finite fields), the ℓ-adic cycle class map from CH²(A)⊗Q_ℓ onto the Galois-invariant part of H⁴_ét(A_k̄, Q_ℓ(2)) is surjective, for ℓ not equal to the characteristic. This is codimension 2 as the text reads. A search-result summary of the paper also says codimension 3 follows from the divisor case by hard Lefschetz; I did not verify that in the text I read.
events.remains: Abelian varieties of dimensions other than four; non-abelian varieties; Tate's second conjecture. The paper also claims standard conjecture D for abelian fourfolds over arbitrary fields, which is not part of the Tate statement.
events.time_since_posted: About eight weeks (19 August to 13 October 2026). No public engagement by a qualified mathematician found in the searches I ran; the only checking reported is the author's own.
events.doubts: (1) Single author, no venue, no referee or Lean certificate found; the only checking the paper reports is by the author ('independently checked by the author'). (2) The method was suggested by an unnamed LLM and then restructured by the author, who says the drafts had 'a number of errors and gaps'; whether the final text is error-free is not reported. (3) The argument depends on Markman's Weil-class theorem and on Ancona's exotic-classes analysis; an error in either would propagate. Neither has been reported in error. (4) Two later preprints by Ningyi Li that use this paper's theorem were withdrawn on 8 October 2026; the withdrawal notices do not name Broe's paper or give a mathematical reason (see those events). (5) The 'stabilization' idea is named in this paper; OpenAI's withdrawn Weil-classes manuscript was invalidated by an error in a 'stabilization-trace cancellation argument'. The terms overlap, but I found no source connecting the two arguments.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirms it for abelian fourfolds over finite fields (codimension 2, as the text reads).

systems.name: a large language model
systems.what_it_did: Per the author's disclosure: the model was used 'to explore proof strategies, to locate relevant literature, to critically examine mathematical arguments, and to assist with copyediting and LaTeX typesetting'. The author first asked it to try to use Markman's results to prove Theorem 1.1; in the ensuing interaction it suggested a method involving Ancona's analysis of exotic classes and the 'stabilization' idea. The author then developed and restructured that strategy, corrected errors and gaps, and based the proof on Chow motives with a motivic technique that simplified the last step. The paper does not say which parts of the final proof derive from the suggestion. The model is not named (footnote: the author opted not to identify it).
systems.basis_quote: In the ensuing interaction, the model suggested a method involving Ancona's analysis of exotic classes and the 'stabilization' idea discussed in Remark 1.4.

events.what_happened: Ningyi Li (University of Regensburg), 'The Tate conjecture for abelian fivefolds over finite fields', arXiv 2609.06265. v1 5 September 2026; v2 10 September 2026; v3 8 October 2026, withdrawn (1 KB). The v2 abstract: 'We prove the Tate conjecture for abelian fivefolds over finite fields.' Per the abstract, the proof constructs correspondences for a residual motive using a Moret–Bailly family, Gross–Schoen heights and monodromy. Theorem 1.1 as read (garbled text): for an abelian fivefold over a finite field F_q, for each 0 ≤ r ≤ 5 and prime ℓ ≠ p, the cycle class map from CH^r(A)⊗Q_ℓ onto the Frobenius-invariant part of H^{2r}_ét(A_F̄_q, Q_ℓ(r)) is surjective. Acknowledgements (v2 HTML): 'The author used OpenAI Codex for literature searches, exploration of proof strategies, reference verification, proof auditing, and LaTeX formatting.' The bibliography cites Broe's fourfold preprint.
events.delivers: As posted (v1 and v2): the Tate conjecture for abelian fivefolds over finite fields in every codimension 0 to 5. The manuscript has been withdrawn, so it establishes nothing as it stands.
events.remains: Abelian varieties of other dimensions; non-abelian varieties; Tate's second conjecture.
events.time_since_posted: Withdrawn by its author about five weeks after posting (5 September to 8 October 2026). No public engagement found.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author. The v3 comment reads 'Withdrawn by the author following a reassessment of the paper's contribution.' The author says they no longer plan a standalone paper and will develop selected methods in a separate one. The reason is not stated in terms of a mathematical error.

withdrawn.what: Withdrawn by the author (v3, 8 October 2026): 'Withdrawn by the author following a reassessment of the paper's contribution.' The author no longer plans to publish it as a standalone paper.

events.direction: Would confirm the Tate conjecture for abelian fivefolds if the withdrawn text were correct; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Ningyi Li (University of Regensburg), 'The Tate conjecture for powers of abelian fourfolds and the Hodge conjecture for powers of CM fourfolds', arXiv 2609.27916. v1 dated 10 September 2026 by the arXiv page (the identifier number suggests a later date in September; I did not resolve this); v2 8 October 2026, withdrawn (1 KB). Claims, per the abstract as read: Tate in every codimension for every power A^n of an abelian variety A of dimension at most four over a finite field (geometrically simple fourfolds via Broe's theorem; dihedral pairs of abelian surfaces via the Gross–Schoen height formula); and the Hodge conjecture for every power of a complex CM abelian fourfold (via Markman's Weil-class theorem and Milne's criterion). Acknowledgements (v1 HTML): 'The author used OpenAI Codex for literature searches, exploration of proof strategies, reference verification, proof auditing, and LaTeX formatting.' Withdrawal comment: 'Withdrawn by the author following a reassessment of the paper's contribution in light of recent work on the Hodge and Tate conjectures for abelian varieties.'

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (repository preprint, released in the openai/math repository on 6 October 2026, within a batch of 722 manuscripts; news reports date the paper 30 September 2026, its TeX source is dated 6 October 2026, and the README's version note links a 30 September version). Abstract (the TeX source of the build folder, read via a fetch tool): 'We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication: every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes. As consequences, we obtain the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.' The repository's catalogue entry (CONTENTS.md, read via a fetch tool) says: 'Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields.' Wikipedia's Tate article cites the OpenAI catalogue (6 October 2026) for the statement that one manuscript 'claims the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, in all dimensions, codimensions and characteristics'. The author line is 'OpenAI'; no human is named. The repository's history file (7 October 2026) does not list this manuscript as withdrawn.
events.revisions: Build folder dated 6 October 2026 (main.tex \date); the README's version note says it 'updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection' and links a 30 September 2026 version. I could not establish that a copy was publicly posted before the 6 October release, so the date may instead be 6 October 2026.
events.delivers: The Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields, in all dimensions, codimensions and characteristics, as a corollary of the claimed Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties via Milne's theorems (per CONTENTS.md and the abstract). Milne's reduction (Hodge for all CM abelian varieties over C implies Tate for abelian varieties over finite fields) is conditional, so the Tate claim stands or falls with the CM Hodge claim. Its scope as a Tate statement is the class of abelian varieties over finite fields.
events.remains: Tate for smooth projective varieties that are not abelian; Tate's second conjecture; and the full Hodge conjecture for non-CM varieties, which the manuscript does not claim.
events.time_since_posted: About seven days (6 to 13 October 2026). No qualified public reading found. AIProofWatch says the Hodge entry has had no independent checking and the Tate result is not yet independently validated; an advisory group reported in a news article said its advice 'does not mean it endorsed the method' and that its role 'should not be interpreted as a judgment of the impact of these results'. Neither is a verification.
events.doubts: (1) The author line is 'OpenAI' and the manuscript was produced by an internal model; no human has put a name to it. (2) The README says results are 'at different stages of verification' and that 'some of the unformalized results could have issues'. (3) News summaries say the CM Hodge result has no Lean formalization and that 032 has no Lean link in the catalogue; the lean/formalization.yaml file returned no Hodge or Tate entries. (4) The Tate claim is derivative: it is only as sound as the CM Hodge argument and Milne's conditional reduction. (5) The README lists this result among 'exceptions to this fixed procedure' used for most results; the README does not, in what I read, say how it was produced. (6) Three other manuscripts were withdrawn on 7 October 2026 (see the Weil-classes event); this one is not among them, but whether it depends on the withdrawn constructions is not stated in anything I read. (7) Milne's own public view of the OpenAI use was not found.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: claims Tate I for all abelian varieties over finite fields, conditionally on the CM Hodge claim it depends on.
events.object: No explicit object. The main result is a proof that every rational Hodge class on a complex CM abelian variety is a rational combination of algebraic cycle classes; the Tate consequence is derived from it via Milne. The abstract describes no explicit construction.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 the Tate conjecture has not been proved in general, and I found no source saying it has. The movement is in the abelian-variety case over finite fields and in a handful of partial cases; the 2026 claims are the main news. (a) Matt Broe, sole author, arXiv 2608.28651 (19 August 2026), claims the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finite fields (codimension 2 as the text reads). The paper's disclosure says a large language model, not named (a footnote says the author chose not to identify it), suggested the 'stabilization' method that the author then restructured and corrected; the author says all statements and references were checked by the author alone. (b) OpenAI's catalogue entry for 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (news reports date it 30 September 2026; its TeX source is dated 6 October; released in the openai/math repository on 6 October 2026) claims that Hodge theorem, and the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields as a corollary through Milne's theorems. The author line is 'OpenAI' and the work is credited to 'an internal OpenAI model'. The README lists the Hodge result among the exceptions to the procedure used for most of the 722 manuscripts, says some unformalized results 'could have issues', and I found no Lean link for it. Milne's 1999 reduction is conditional (Hodge for all CM abelian varieties over C implies Tate for abelian varieties over finite fields), so the OpenAI Tate claim stands or falls with the CM Hodge claim. (c) Ningyi Li posted Tate claims for abelian fivefolds (5 September 2026) and for powers of abelian fourfolds (10 September 2026); both disclose use of 'OpenAI Codex' (the disclosed uses are literature search, 'exploration of proof strategies', reference verification, proof auditing and LaTeX), and both were withdrawn by the author on 8 October 2026 for reasons given only as a 'reassessment of the paper's contribution'. Neither withdrawal names a mathematical error. OpenAI also withdrew three manuscripts on 7 October 2026 (a Weil-classes paper and two dependent papers) for a sign error in a 'stabilization-trace cancellation argument'; the CM Hodge manuscript is not among them per the repository's history file, and whether it depends on those constructions is not stated in anything I read. Searches to 13 October 2026 found no public check by a qualified mathematician of the Broe or the OpenAI Tate claims, and Milne's own view of the OpenAI use was not found. Partial, non-AI events in the window: Guo–Yang on surfaces of geometric genus one (January 2025; 'largely complete', v2 'major revision'); Arango-Piñeros–Frengley–Vemulapalli, new cases including non-maximal angle rank (May 2025); Broe's Beilinson–Bloch paper, which claims new Tate cases over finite fields (September 2025); Hamacher–Yang–Zhao's generic divisor case (first posted 2022, final 2025); Schreieder's Milnor K-theory reformulation (June 2024) and Kahn's reformulation with three failed approaches (May 2025), which prove nothing. Variants are recorded and discounted: integral-Tate counterexamples (Scavia–Suzuki 2022, Cadoret–Pirutka 2024 conditional, Suzuki talk 2024, Milne 2025, and the older Kameko and Antieau papers), a logarithmic analogue (Kato–Nakayama–Usui 2025), and a Brauer-group expository note (Feng 2026). Predating the window, the K3 and abelian-variety cases were already established in part: Charles 2012, Madapusi Pera 2013, Ito–Ito–Koshikawa 2018 (K3 squares in all characteristics), Yang 2021, Milne 1999 and 2021, and Li–Zhang 2021. The Markman Weil-class paper (February 2025) is Hodge-side and is discounted, though Broe's and Li's papers use it. Close calls for the later pass: (i) the date of OpenAI 032 (30 September dated, 6 October public); (ii) whether Broe's 'stabilization' method has any link to the withdrawn argument (none found; terminology overlaps only); (iii) whether Li's withdrawals respond to Broe, to OpenAI, or to neither; (iv) Broe's Theorem 1.1 as read says 'a field k' while the title and abstract say finite fields; (v) whether an abelian case over finite fields counts as a case of the bullet, which the bullet's wording (all varieties) supports. Two cross-checks: the OpenAI README shows 719 manuscripts after three withdrawals, consistent with the 722 at release; and the Wikipedia article's wording ('one of which claims') is looser than the catalogue's 'this also gives', which is a corollary.
competing_reading: Read as a real advance: Broe's fourfold proof is a complete argument by a named mathematician who says he checked it; the Milne reduction it parallels is an existing 1999 theorem; if OpenAI's CM Hodge proof stands, the abelian-variety case over finite fields is settled in every dimension, and Broe's result is then a special case. Read as no advance yet: no referee, no Lean certificate for the OpenAI Hodge result, the OpenAI release carries its own warning about unformalized results and had three withdrawals in its first day, and the Li papers in the same area were withdrawn within a month. On this reading the OpenAI Tate claim adds nothing independent, because it is a corollary of an unchecked Hodge theorem. A third reading concerns scope: every reading leaves the general Tate conjecture open, so the question is whether a fixed-dimension or all-dimensions result for abelian varieties counts as a case of this bullet. The bullet says 'algebraic varieties' without restriction, which supports counting it as a case, but the later pass should decide that rather than inherit my reading.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An expert written verification, or a published error report, on Broe's arXiv 2608.28651, especially its codimension-2 Theorem 1.1 and its use of Markman's Weil-class theorem and Ancona's exotic-classes analysis. (2) A human or Lean check of the OpenAI CM Hodge manuscript (repository folder preprints/The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-October-6-2026), together with its entry in the repository's history file for any change. (3) Milne's own statement on whether his reduction applies to the CM Hodge claim as OpenAI states it, and in all degrees. (4) The text of the footnote in Broe's paper that cross-refers to a prior paper's footnote on not naming the model; that prior paper would show what the author meant. (5) Ningyi Li's reason for withdrawal, in particular whether it refers to Broe's or to OpenAI's result. (6) Whether the OpenAI Hodge manuscript depends on any of the three withdrawn constructions, which the history file would show if it names dependencies. (7) Any later paper that states Tate for all abelian varieties over finite fields as established and cites a reviewed source, or that reports an error in either the Broe or the OpenAI argument.

incomplete: (1) Broe's paper: I read the arXiv HTML through a fetch tool, which returned the disclosure and acknowledgements verbatim, and quoted pieces of Theorem 1.1 with a paraphrase. The full text beyond about 100,000 characters was not read, so the proof, the codimension-3 claim (reported in a search summary, not verified) and the footnote text are incomplete. The footnote's cross-reference to a prior paper's footnote was not resolved. (2) OpenAI's CM Hodge manuscript: the PDF and the TeX section files were not readable (the build folder returned the preamble and abstract only). The Tate corollary's wording comes from the CONTENTS.md entry and the abstract as the fetch tool returned them; its proof was not read, and the README's paragraph on the procedure used for this manuscript was summarised, not quoted in full. (3) The openai.com announcement returned HTTP 403, and the searchable catalogue was too large to fetch, so the entry-level metadata for the Tate corollary rests on CONTENTS.md. (4) Milne's 1999 and 2001 papers were not readable as PDFs; their statements come from Milne's 2021 abstract. (5) Li's two papers: the fivefold's Theorem 1.1 text was garbled in the source, and the fourfold-powers text was only partly read (the first 100,000 characters).
